328ee10.summary: Called after an effect finishes that clears end-of-turn effects on the acting card: clears them, then runs the shared post-action cleanup. The cleanup queues minion reassembly, ends the battle if a hero is dying, and re-enables the current turn owner's units and UI.
comments: Only clear end-of-turn effects if an acting card was supplied.
Count pending queued actions; the cleanup below only runs when the queue is drained.
Queue empty: if either side's minions have drifted out of position, queue a reassemble order for them.
No automatic follow-up actions pending: safe to check whether a hero has died.
Tutorial and campaign matches skip the hero-death check here.
Card state 5 appears to mean waitingToDie; if neither hero is dying, jump to the normal in-play broadcast.
A hero is dying; remember whether it was the local player's (player lost) or the enemy's.
Builds a debug log line 'called DeadHeroAfterActionsEnd ...' (inlined; decompiler bloat with array bounds checks).
Battle already in PostBattle: warn and return, unless the disconnect-loss flag is set.
Disconnect-loss flag set: record an enemy victory and run the battle end sequence coroutine instead.
Normal battle end: enter PostBattle stage and stop the battle.
In a networked game, tell the other player the match has finished.
Lock the UI into the finish-battle sequence and clear the during-battle flag.
Player won: raise an enemy-health-change signal showing the enemy hero's health being brought to 0.
Build a RankedMatchResult from Elo rating (event leaderboard or player data) and XP, plus skull milestones.
Work out the winner from who lost and the battle result.
Record the match duration; if the player won, flag the win in player data and update the live-ops handler.
Persist the match winner and finish the battle; the cleanup below is not reached in this path.
Decompiler artifact: an index/cast failure path after the nested checks.
No hero is dying: broadcast while-in-play effects so continuous effects are re-evaluated.
Action fully resolved: clear the resolving-action flag.
Whose turn is it? Enemy's turn refreshes the enemy side, player's turn refreshes the player side.
Enemy turn: activate enemy minions and recompute whether the enemy hero can act or attack.
Hero can act only if it is in play, hasn't attacked (or has bloodthirst and attacked once), is not stunned, and isn't summon-sick.
Ferocity or oath heroes get canAct set again, and switch to an active attack type if summon-sick.
Show or hide the hero's can-attack animation on its card UI depending on whether it can attack now.
Player's turn: highlight playable cards and re-activate the player's minions and hero.
Check how many actions remain in the queue.
Queue empty: start garbage collection while idle and unpause the turn clock.
If the player may act, gather the available actions.
Only one action (end turn) left and not forced by tutorial: show the 'no actions left' UI on the clock.
Re-check the queue after the above.
Scripted (tutorial/AI-script) stage: if the script is waiting for a player action, continue the scripted turn.
Reset the flag that remembers a manual player action happened in this action sequence.

328eea0.summary: Resolves a stun battle action: applies the stun to the target unit and, if it worked, broadcasts that the unit was stunned. It then calls FinishResolvingAction for the action type. Called when a queued stun action is processed.
comments: Copy the action (0x100 bytes) and apply the stun to the target unit for the current turn owner.
Stun succeeded: broadcast the unit-stunned event so abilities can react.
Mark the action as resolved and let the queue continue.
Null target in the action: decompiler's null-check throw.

328f19c.summary: Destroys a unit: if it is in the waiting-to-die state it triggers backlash and, if needed, queues a transform into a remnant. Then runs the shared post-action cleanup: minion reassembly, hero death/battle end, and re-enabling the turn owner's units and UI.
comments: Unit to destroy (named isPlayer by the decompiler, but it is a CardScript); missing unit means the null-check path.
Card state 5 (waitingToDie) is required to destroy; otherwise log a warning at the else-branch below.
Some units turn into a remnant instead of simply dying.
If this flag byte is non-zero, skip the remnant transform and just trigger backlash.
Unit is dying: trigger its backlash actions, then queue the transform into a remnant.
No remnant: only trigger backlash actions for the dying unit.
Wrong state: log 'Can't DestroyUnit <name> because state is ...' and do nothing.
Remember the action type; reorderMinionsInPlay must not queue another reassemble.
Queue empty (and not already a reorder): queue reassembly for any misplaced minions on either side.
No automatic actions pending: check whether a hero has died.
Tutorial and campaign matches skip the hero-death check here.
